body.statement: The tensor criterion has the following reductions. For \((G_{\mathrm{bow}},S_{\mathrm{diag}})\), it rejects identification of \(P_{\operatorname{do}(X=1)}(Y=1)\). For \((G_{\mathrm{IV}},S_{\mathrm{IV5}})\), it identifies \(P_{\operatorname{do}(X=0)}(Y=1)=P(X=0,Y=1\mid Z=1)\). When \(S=\mathcal X_V\), every classically identified query is accepted and the rational functional agrees with the classical identifying functional on positive laws.
body.justification: These controls prevent factual equalities or unsupported cancellations from masquerading as intervention identities.
body.gap: The five-cell identity and diagonal-bow rejection are not supplied by formula-level positivity checks as a paired completeness diagnostic.
body.consumer: They provide minimal regression tests for any implementation and recover the familiar full-support regime.
body.proof_tex:
For the diagonal bow, let \(U\) be a fair binary root for its single district.  In the first SCM set
\[
X=U,\qquad Y=U,
\]
and in the second set
\[
X=U,\qquad Y=X.
\]
Both structural assignments respect \(G_{\mathrm{bow}}\), both have factual law assigning probability \(1/2\) to each element of \(S_{\mathrm{diag}}\), and neither assigns mass outside that support.  Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=1)\), however,
\[
P(Y=1)=\frac12
\quad\text{in the first SCM},
\qquad
P(Y=1)=1
\quad\text{in the second SCM}.                                \tag{27}
\]
Thus the query is not uniformly identified.  By the uniform-identification tensor-span theorem, the tensor criterion rejects it.  This also shows explicitly why the factual equality \(Y=X\) on the diagonal support cannot be substituted after intervention.

For the five-cell instrumental-variable control, the districts are \(\{Z\}\) and \(\{X,Y\}\).  Write a downstream response type as
\[
(x_0,x_1,y_0,y_1),
\]
where \(x_z\) is the response of \(X\) to \(Z=z\), and \(y_x\) is the response of \(Y\) to \(X=x\).  Applying the first-forbidden-prefix conditions to \(S_{\mathrm{IV5}}\) gives exactly the following downstream saturated types:
\[
\begin{array}{cc}
(0,0,0,0),&(0,0,0,1),\\
(0,1,0,1),&(1,0,0,0),\\
(1,0,1,0).&
\end{array}                                                     \tag{28}
\]
To verify (28), when \(z=0\), factual support permits \((x,y)=(0,0)\) and \((1,0)\), forcing \(y_0=0\) if \(x_0=0\) and \(y_1=0\) if \(x_0=1\).  When \(z=1\), it permits \((0,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), imposing no restriction on \(y_0\) if \(x_1=0\) and forcing \(y_1=1\) if \(x_1=1\).  Combining the four possibilities for \((x_0,x_1)\) yields precisely the five types in (28), with the case \((1,1)\) impossible because it would require both \(y_1=0\) and \(y_1=1\).

Inspection of (28) gives the pointwise response identity
\[
\mathbf 1\{y_0=1\}
=\mathbf 1\{x_1=0,\ y_{x_1}=1\}.                              \tag{29}
\]
The left side of (29) is the outcome indicator under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).  The right side is the indicator of \(\{X=0,Y=1\}\) under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=1)\).  The root for \(Z\) is independent of the downstream root, so conditioning factually on \(Z=1\) leaves the downstream root law unchanged.  Because \(S_{\mathrm{IV5}}\) contains cells with \(Z=1\), exact support gives \(P(Z=1)>0\).  Taking expectations in (29) therefore yields
\[
P_{\operatorname{do}(X=0)}(Y=1)
=P_{\operatorname{do}(Z=1)}(X=0,Y=1)
=P(X=0,Y=1\mid Z=1).                                          \tag{30}
\]
Thus this query is uniformly identified and the tensor criterion accepts it by the equivalence theorem.  Equation (30), including its positive conditional denominator, is the asserted five-cell functional.

Finally, suppose \(S=\mathcal X_V\) and a query is classically identified for \(G\).  By the meaning of classical identification, any two graph-compatible SCMs having the same observational law have the same query value.  This implication applies in particular to the canonical independent-district-root subclass \(\Theta_S\).  Uniform identification on this exact full-support face follows, so the tensor criterion accepts the query.  On every positive graph-compatible law, the classical functional and the rational functional supplied by the rational-functional theorem both equal the same interventional target; hence they agree there.  No equality away from the graph-compatible observational model is required.
